title: How a Diving Bell Spider Breathes Underwater | Toxic Tales
description:
How does a spider breathe underwater?

The diving bell spider (Argyroneta aquatica) builds a silk-supported pocket of air among freshwater plants. Oxygen dissolved in the surrounding water can diffuse into this bell, helping it act as a physical gill.

Seymour and Hetz measured oxygen and gas exchange in laboratory diving bells. Many bells supplied enough oxygen for resting spiders in warm, still aquarium water. But nitrogen escapes, the chamber shrinks, and the spider eventually needs fresh surface air. These results do not establish oxygen supply for every active spider or every natural habitat.

TT-006 | Original research:
Seymour, R. S. & Hetz, S. K. (2011). The diving bell and the spider: the physical gill of Argyroneta aquatica. Journal of Experimental Biology 214:2175–2181.
